title: Now from the Altar of Our Hearts
description: Now from the Altar of Our Hearts in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 508, “Family Evening Worship”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Now from the al-tar of our hearts Let war-mest thanks a-rise; As-sist us, Lord, to o-ffer up Our eve-ning sac-ri-fice.

lines: Now from the altar of our hearts
Assist us, Lord, to offer up
This day our God has been our sun,
His arm around our weakness thrown,
Have made up all the day;
Moments came fast, but mercies were
More swift and free than they.
New hours, new blessings, and new joys,
Till we can praise Thee as we should,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1866.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
